propositions: The rebar-implement skill subagent in Phase 4d lacks explicit model tier specification and inherits the orchestrator's expensive model tier by default, negating cost savings.
The skill provides no guidance on which work is safe to delegate to cheaper models versus which requires strong-tier capabilities, or how to escalate when cheaper models fail.
A capability-tiered model delegation framework with abstract tier names (strong/standard/cheap) must map to concrete Claude Code and Codex CLI examples without hardcoding product model names.
The held-out-TDD invariant (test authoring and held-out validation remain strong-tier, implementer is separate) must be preserved under the new tiering scheme.
Phase 3 dispatch-by-kind, Phase 4a search strategy, Phase 4d implementation defaults, and a new 4e-bis escalation ladder must be amended to implement consistent tiering policy.
